message.content: {"summary":"A well-structured, fluent ethics report with balanced arguments, relevant case studies (NHS, Volkswagen) and a clear, justified recommendation. Your stakeholder analysis and evidence are strong, but the report lacks any visual elements, has minor typos, and reference formatting is inconsistent.","next_steps":["Add visual elements such as a stakeholder table or decision-flow diagram to support your discussion and lift C5.","Resolve open arguments (e.g. whether competitors would ship defective products anyway) rather than leaving them hanging.","Broaden decision-making recommendations to more stakeholders (chip contractor, government health department) and add counter-evidence and more sources.","Fix reference formatting to consistent IEEE style, including URLs and access dates, and proofread headings/typos."],"criteria":{"C1":"Excellent: you identified several ethical issues (public safety, integrity, business ethics), linked them to engineering design, and clearly demonstrated both organisational context and stakeholder interests in your Introduction. Maintain this breadth in future work.","C2":"Very good: your for/against arguments have appropriate depth and a clear conclusion, but decision-making recommendations cover mainly Rachel and her company. To reach Excellent, extend recommendations to other stakeholders such as the chip contractor and the health department.","C3":"Very good: your body builds logically from economic to safety, integrity and reputation arguments and supports your conclusion well. To reach Excellent, resolve open arguments (e.g. the competitor-shipping point) so every thread strengthens the conclusion.","C4":"Very good: the NHS and Volkswagen case studies with quantitative evidence substantiate your arguments well. To reach Excellent, use more sources and include counter-evidence to show a fully balanced, in-depth research base.","C5":"Good: your writing is fluent with all required sections, but there are no figures, tables or visual elements, plus minor typos (e.g. 'DICUSSION') and inconsistent IEEE reference formatting. Adding visuals and polishing formatting would lift this substantially."}}
